content.content: {"result":"{\"mimeType\": \"text/markdown\", \"text\": \"# LLC ground rules (Combo Fighter and whatever else we take)\\nThis is the lifestyle route I posted about in #executives. The LLC is the new one Blake and I are setting up for the three of us, and anything Harmony Games owns (the games with their art and listings, and the equipment) comes to it only through Sunset's sale, the way I wrote after the call on Wednesday. Services we keep running just move their billing to the LLC.\\nThe plan runs March 1 to May 31.\\nDomino Delights and Zombie Match come over only if what each made in January, going by the warehouse's daily revenue table, covers what its own hosting bills now, whatever we said about them before. Combo Fighter comes over either way, it's the reason we're doing this. A game that comes over brings what it needs to keep running, its accounts and its player support.\\nCost every item at what it bills now, going by whoever runs it, not by what HG used to pay.\\nWhat we already decided to keep or cancel for the shutdown in #winddown stays decided.\\nPay for anyone who stays on is a separate conversation once we know the running cost; this plan is only what bills us every month, no one-offs or yearly fees.\\nHow things move is on the LLC card on our board.\\n\", \"id\": \"f_1e468a9d69ea0f0a2001f5\", \"name\": \"LLC ground rules (Combo Fighter and whatever else we take)\"}"}

{"mimeType": "text/markdown", "text": "# LLC ground rules (Combo Fighter and whatever else we take)
This is the lifestyle route I posted about in #executives. The LLC is the new one Blake and I are setting up for the three of us, and anything Harmony Games owns (the games with their art and listings, and the equipment) comes to it only through Sunset's sale, the way I wrote after the call on Wednesday. Services we keep running just move their billing to the LLC.
The plan runs March 1 to May 31.
Domino Delights and Zombie Match come over only if what each made in January, going by the warehouse's daily revenue table, covers what its own hosting bills now, whatever we said about them before. Combo Fighter comes over either way, it's the reason we're doing this. A game that comes over brings what it needs to keep running, its accounts and its player support.
Cost every item at what it bills now, going by whoever runs it, not by what HG used to pay.
What we already decided to keep or cancel for the shutdown in #winddown stays decided.
Pay for anyone who stays on is a separate conversation once we know the running cost; this plan is only what bills us every month, no one-offs or yearly fees.
How things move is on the LLC card on our board.
", "id": "f_1e468a9d69ea0f0a2001f5", "name": "LLC ground rules (Combo Fighter and whatever else we take)"}

Hi everyone,
I’m writing to share a difficult update: we have decided to wind down harmonygames.
We reached this decision after a thorough review of the most recent data across our products and the realistic set of options in front of us. Despite multiple iterations, we did not get the metrics to a point that supports a viable business path, and we do not have the funding to continue operating while searching for a new direction.
What we did and what we learned
• We built and tested three games on a limited budget, staying true to our mission of hybridcasual gameplay with RPG depth.
• We took real creative risks and pushed to innovate:
Domino Delights: Domino/Tripeak solitaire gameplay with RPG elements
Zombie Match 3D: Match Factory style core loop with RPG combat/progression elements
Combo Fighter: Tetris-like block gameplay with RPG elements
• We also explored partnerships and other paths to scale distribution and improve outcomes, but none changed the trajectory enough.
Financial context
• We have been in sustained financial hardship since mid-2025.
• Revenue did not reach meaningful levels, and the plans we pursued to change that did not work.
• Given our current runway of less than a month and obligations, continuing would create risk without a responsible probability of success.
What happens next
• We are initiating an orderly wind-down process and preparing the required board resolutions and documentation.
• Our priorities are to handle employee and contractor obligations properly, meet tax and compliance requirements, close out vendor commitments, and Sunset the products in a controlled way.
• We will also evaluate what to do with the remaining IP and codebase (archive, sale, or other disposition) and will keep you informed.
Timeline and updates
• We will share a more detailed wind-down plan and timeline shortly, including key dates for operational shutdown.
• I will send periodic updates as we complete the major steps and once we have clarity on final liabilities and any remaining assets.
I regret having to send this. I am proud of the team we put together and the quality of what we shipped. We ran a frugal operation, made multiple bets, and pushed hard, but we did not reach the performance required to build a durable company.
If you would like to talk 1:1 this week, reply here and I will make time.
Thank you,

Which competitors does this title sit next to?*\\nOn mobile, this title sits closest to:\\n\\u2022 The Sims (Freeplay / Mobile): deep life simulation and expression.\\n\\u2022 Cozy idle sims such as Cats & Soup and similar \\u201cwatch your world run\\u201d games.\\n\\u2022 Lifestyle and decor titles in the home design and fashion space.\\nThe key difference: we are effectively offering a \\u201cquick simulation\\u201d button for Barbie life moments. Every action is designed to resolve in short, satisfying sessions that fit mobile: start a career shift, run a mini day in Barbieland, complete a micro story, then step away.\\nWe borrow some loop structure from idle clickers to keep Barbie\\u2019s world running in the background, but unlike pure idle titles, this game adds roleplay, story context, and character identity on top of those systems. The result is closer to a \\u201csnackable Sims in Barbieland\\u201d than a standard clicker.\\n\\n*2. What gap in the market are you aiming to fill?*\\nThere is no mobile experience today that gives Barbie fans a living, evergreen Barbieland where they can:\\n\\u2022 Collect across the full, ever evolving Barbie universe, not just one product line.\\n\\u2022 Test drive careers, lifestyles, and aesthetics in a low friction, low cost way.\\n\\u2022 Return daily to see their Barbieland grow and change with the brand.\\nThe gap is a \\u201cBarbie lovers universe\\u201d that goes much deeper than a single dress up app or one Dreamhouse. This concept lets fans continuously engage with more facets of Barbie, and live those fantasies digitally at a fraction of the cost of physical collecting, while still driving demand for the physical line.\\n\\n*3. How does this differ from Dreamhouse Adventures, Miniverse, Toca Boca, etc.?*\\n\\u2022 *Dreamhouse Adventures:* Centered on one location and one core fantasy loop. Our concept treats the Dreamhouse as one important module inside a larger Barbieland, with careers, locations, and storylines that expand well beyond the house.\\n\\u2022 *Miniverse:* Focuses on miniature making and ASMR style crafting. We are designing a life sim where the mechanics, aesthetics, and progression are specifically tuned to Barbie\\u2019s brand promise and fanbase.\\nIn short, the IP to genre fit is unique. Which competitors does this title sit next to?*\\nOn mobile, this title sits closest to:\\n\\u2022 The Sims (Freeplay / Mobile): deep life simulation and expression.\\n\\u2022 Cozy idle sims such as Cats & Soup and similar \\u201cwatch your world run\\u201d games.\\n\\u2022 Lifestyle and decor titles in the home design and fashion space.\\nThe key difference: we are effectively offering a \\u201cquick simulation\\u201d button for Barbie life moments. Every action is designed to resolve in short, satisfying sessions that fit mobile: start a career shift, run a mini day in Barbieland, complete a micro story, then step away.\\nWe borrow some loop structure from idle clickers to keep Barbie\\u2019s world running in the background, but unlike pure idle titles, this game adds roleplay, story context, and character identity on top of those systems. The result is closer to a \\u201csnackable Sims in Barbieland\\u201d than a standard clicker.\\n\\n*2. What gap in the market are you aiming to fill?*\\nThere is no mobile experience today that gives Barbie fans a living, evergreen Barbieland where they can:\\n\\u2022 Collect across the full, ever evolving Barbie universe, not just one product line.\\n\\u2022 Test drive careers, lifestyles, and aesthetics in a low friction, low cost way.\\n\\u2022 Return daily to see their Barbieland grow and change with the brand.\\nThe gap is a \\u201cBarbie lovers universe\\u201d that goes much deeper than a single dress up app or one Dreamhouse. This concept lets fans continuously engage with more facets of Barbie, and live those fantasies digitally at a fraction of the cost of physical collecting, while still driving demand for the physical line.\\n\\n*3. How does this differ from Dreamhouse Adventures, Miniverse, Toca Boca, etc.?*\\n\\u2022 *Dreamhouse Adventures:* Centered on one location and one core fantasy loop. Our concept treats the Dreamhouse as one important module inside a larger Barbieland, with careers, locations, and storylines that expand well beyond the house.\\n\\u2022 *Miniverse:* Focuses on miniature making and ASMR style crafting. We take some sensory inspiration, but our core is life simulation and roleplay: what Barbie does with those worlds once they exist.\\n\\u2022 *Toca Boca:* Fantastic at open ended play for kids, but genre agnostic and not rooted in Barbie\\u2019s IP or audience. We are designing a life sim where the mechanics, aesthetics, and progression are specifically tuned to Barbie\\u2019s brand promise and fanbase.\\nIn short, the IP to genre fit is unique. We are not putting Barbie on top of an existing mechanic. We are building systems that express what Barbie stands for in play: choice of path, creativity, and \\u201cyou can be anything.\\u201d\\n\\n*4. What is the aspirational hook that makes this uniquely Barbie?*\\nThe hook: \\u201cBuild your own Barbieland and live every \\u2018you can be anything\\u2019 fantasy inside it.\\u201d\\nA few pillars support that:\\n\\u2022 *More than one thing to do:* Players can move fluidly between careers, hobbies, fashion, travel, and social stories, just like kids do with the dolls.\\n\\u2022 *Modular and combinable:* Each play module (career tracks, locations, collections, events) snaps together, so your Barbieland feels personal and assembled, not scripted from a single storyline.\\n\\u2022 *Player chosen life paths:* The core loop reinforces the founding philosophy of Barbie: players project their own fantasy into the character and choose their own path, adventure, and profession.\\nThat combination of multi path aspiration plus real systems depth is something only Barbie can authentically own in this space.\\n\\n*5. How does this respond to current cozy sim and lifestyle trends?*\\nThe concept is built directly on top of what is working in cozy and lifestyle sims today:\\n\\u2022 Low pressure, low failure, high comfort play.\\n\\u2022 Strong focus on aesthetics, collection, and decoration that feels shareable and aspirational.\\n\\u2022 Light idle elements that reward coming back often without demanding long sessions.\\n\\u2022 High quality sensory feedback: soft animations, satisfying loops, ASMR like interactions.\\nWe then layer Barbie\\u2019s IP and audience targeting on top:\\n\\u2022 The fantasy and visual language map perfectly to the existing cozy and lifestyle audience, but filtered through Barbie\\u2019s world.\\n\\u2022 The brand gives us a more efficient route to the right players. With Barbie front and center, we can acquire fans at a lower CPI than a generic cozy sim, since the game speaks directly to a known, motivated segment.\\nIn effect, we take Proven cozy and idle patterns, align them tightly with Barbie\\u2019s brand promise, and use the IP to reach the exact audience that already craves this kind of experience.\", \"channel\": \"C09QDMC3UL9\", \"user\": \"EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID\", \"thread_ts\": \"1764867254.892579\", \"channel_info\": {\"id\": \"C09QDMC3UL9\", \"name\": \"mattel_proposal\", \"is_private\": true, \"is_im\": false, \"is_mpim\": false}, \"user_profile\": {\"id\": \"EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID\", \"name\": \"Leonard Hayes\", \"real_name\": \"Leonard Hayes\", \"display_name\": \"Leonard Hayes\", \"email\": \"leonard.hayes@harmonygames.co\"}, \"time\": \"2025-12-08T17:22:42Z\", \"permalink\": \"https://harmonygamesgroup.slack.com/archives/C09QDMC3UL9/p1765214562505549?thread_ts=1764867254.892579&cid=C09QDMC3UL9\"}, {\"ts\": \"1765213543.355689\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"*1. Who is the primary target audience?*\\nThe core audience is teen and adult Barbie fans who already enjoy cozy life sims and light idle games on mobile.\\n\\u2022 Roughly 13 to 55, predominantly female.\\n\\u2022 Strong overlap with players of fashion, home design, and lifestyle sim titles.\\n\\u2022 Comfortable with deeper collection, progression, and event systems, and with free to play economy patterns.\\nA secondary audience is Barbie loving kids around 8 to 12 who will naturally arrive through the brand, siblings, parents, and discovery in app stores. We are not designing the systems around young children, but the experience is friendly and intuitive enough that they can still have fun within safe boundaries.\\nThe product is a free to play idle life sim aimed at a teen plus audience, with meaningful progression, collection, and profession systems to support long term engagement and monetization. Which competitors does this title sit next to?*
On mobile, this title sits closest to:
• The Sims (Freeplay / Mobile): deep life simulation and expression.
• Cozy idle sims such as Cats & Soup and similar “watch your world run” games.
• Lifestyle and decor titles in the home design and fashion space.
The key difference: we are effectively offering a “quick simulation” button for Barbie life moments. Every action is designed to resolve in short, satisfying sessions that fit mobile: start a career shift, run a mini day in Barbieland, complete a micro story, then step away.
We borrow some loop structure from idle clickers to keep Barbie’s world running in the background, but unlike pure idle titles, this game adds roleplay, story context, and character identity on top of those systems. The result is closer to a “snackable Sims in Barbieland” than a standard clicker.

*2. What gap in the market are you aiming to fill?*
There is no mobile experience today that gives Barbie fans a living, evergreen Barbieland where they can:
• Collect across the full, ever evolving Barbie universe, not just one product line.
• Test drive careers, lifestyles, and aesthetics in a low friction, low cost way.
• Return daily to see their Barbieland grow and change with the brand.
The gap is a “Barbie lovers universe” that goes much deeper than a single dress up app or one Dreamhouse. This concept lets fans continuously engage with more facets of Barbie, and live those fantasies digitally at a fraction of the cost of physical collecting, while still driving demand for the physical line.

*3. How does this differ from Dreamhouse Adventures, Miniverse, Toca Boca, etc.?*
• *Dreamhouse Adventures:* Centered on one location and one core fantasy loop. Our concept treats the Dreamhouse as one important module inside a larger Barbieland, with careers, locations, and storylines that expand well beyond the house.
• *Miniverse:* Focuses on miniature making and ASMR style crafting. We take some sensory inspiration, but our core is life simulation and roleplay: what Barbie does with those worlds once they exist.
• *Toca Boca:* Fantastic at open ended play for kids, but genre agnostic and not rooted in Barbie’s IP or audience. We are designing a life sim where the mechanics, aesthetics, and progression are specifically tuned to Barbie’s brand promise and fanbase.
In short, the IP to genre fit is unique. We are not putting Barbie on top of an existing mechanic. We are building systems that express what Barbie stands for in play: choice of path, creativity, and “you can be anything.”

*4. What is the aspirational hook that makes this uniquely Barbie?*
The hook: “Build your own Barbieland and live every ‘you can be anything’ fantasy inside it.”
A few pillars support that:
• *More than one thing to do:* Players can move fluidly between careers, hobbies, fashion, travel, and social stories, just like kids do with the dolls.
• *Modular and combinable:* Each play module (career tracks, locations, collections, events) snaps together, so your Barbieland feels personal and assembled, not scripted from a single storyline.
• *Player chosen life paths:* The core loop reinforces the founding philosophy of Barbie: players project their own fantasy into the character and choose their own path, adventure, and profession.
That combination of multi path aspiration plus real systems depth is something only Barbie can authentically own in this space.

*5. How does this respond to current cozy sim and lifestyle trends?*
The concept is built directly on top of what is working in cozy and lifestyle sims today:
• Low pressure, low failure, high comfort play.
• Strong focus on aesthetics, collection, and decoration that feels shareable and aspirational.
• Light idle elements that reward coming back often without demanding long sessions.
• High quality sensory feedback: soft animations, satisfying loops, ASMR like interactions.
We then layer Barbie’s IP and audience targeting on top:
• The fantasy and visual language map perfectly to the existing cozy and lifestyle audience, but filtered through Barbie’s world.
• The brand gives us a more efficient route to the right players. With Barbie front and center, we can acquire fans at a lower CPI than a generic cozy sim, since the game speaks directly to a known, motivated segment.
In effect, we take Proven cozy and idle patterns, align them tightly with Barbie’s brand promise, and use the IP to reach the exact audience that already craves this kind of experience.", "channel": "C09QDMC3UL9", "user": "EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID", "thread_ts": "1764867254.892579", "channel_info": {"id": "C09QDMC3UL9", "name": "mattel_proposal", "is_private": true, "is_im": false, "is_mpim": false}, "user_profile": {"id": "EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID", "name": "Leonard Hayes", "real_name": "Leonard Hayes", "display_name": "Leonard Hayes", "email": "leonard.hayes@harmonygames.co"}, "time": "2025-12-08T17:22:42Z", "permalink": "https://harmonygamesgroup.slack.com/archives/C09QDMC3UL9/p1765214562505549?thread_ts=1764867254.892579&cid=C09QDMC3UL9"}, {"ts": "1765213543.355689", "type": "message", "text": "*1. Who is the primary target audience?*
The core audience is teen and adult Barbie fans who already enjoy cozy life sims and light idle games on mobile.
• Roughly 13 to 55, predominantly female.
• Strong overlap with players of fashion, home design, and lifestyle sim titles.
• Comfortable with deeper collection, progression, and event systems, and with free to play economy patterns.
A secondary audience is Barbie loving kids around 8 to 12 who will naturally arrive through the brand, siblings, parents, and discovery in app stores. We are not designing the systems around young children, but the experience is friendly and intuitive enough that they can still have fun within safe boundaries.
The product is a free to play idle life sim aimed at a teen plus audience, with meaningful progression, collection, and profession systems to support long term engagement and monetization. At the same time, themes, visuals, and tone stay within PEGI 3 and ESRB E style expectations so that the game remains positive, aspirational, and safe if younger players join.

*2. Is the game built for teens, young adults, or children?*
The design target is teens and young adults, with adults welcome, and children protected.
• Systems depth, economy, and long term goals are tuned for players 13 plus who are used to free to play games and can engage with more complex progression and collection.
• Content, tone, and themes remain family friendly and brand safe, so if an 8 to 12 year old plays alongside an older sibling or parent, the experience still feels appropriate and positive.
This gives Barbie a mobile product that speaks to the broader fandom while staying fully aligned with Mattel standards.

*3. If needed, how would the concept adapt to PEGI 3?*
Our baseline plan is already aligned with PEGI 3 style requirements. If needed, we can go further and tighten around formal PEGI and ESRB guidance in collaboration with your brand and compliance teams. Concretely:
• No bad language, explicit conflict, or frightening imagery.
• No romantic content that would Push the rating beyond PEGI 3.
• Visuals that emphasize colorful, toy like environments instead of realistic intensity.
• Clear UI and parental friendly settings for things like purchases and online features.
We would work directly with the Mattel team and your publishing partner to review early assets, copy, and features, and treat ratings compliance as a core gate at each milestone, not a late stage patch.

I will break down why and how to Push it to the low end.
I am not your lawyer or accountant, so treat this as planning guidance and sanity check, not formal advice.

1. What drives the cost
Key factors that matter for Harmony Games specifically:
1. *Type of company and complexity*
    ◦ Delaware C-corp with investors and a real cap table.
    ◦ Multiple SAFEs / equity holders.
    ◦ Employment / contractor agreements across countries.
    ◦ Multiple commercial contracts (publishers, ad networks, platforms, vendors).
2. More complexity pushes you away from “simple startup dissolution” pricing and into custom work.
3. *Where fees show up*
4.  You are not just paying for “file a dissolution form”:
    ◦ corporate / securities law work.
    ◦ Contract review and termination.
    ◦ Employment and IP issues.
    ◦ Tax and accounting cleanup.
    ◦ Possibly some board / investor process work (consents, releases, etc.).
5. *Your goal*
    ◦ If you want a “clean, defendable shutdown” that future investors and acquirers will not side-eye, you will spend more than the absolute bare minimum.
    ◦ If you are ok with more “duct tape,” you can cut costs, but you increase risk of something biting you later.
2. Rough fee ranges by category
These are order-of-magnitude numbers for a company like yours, using a mix of decent startup counsel + a scrappy accountant, not BigLaw overkill.
A. corporate dissolution & governance: *10k–30k*
Covers things like:
• Board and stockholder approvals.
• Formal dissolution with Delaware, plus any foreign registrations (e.g. NC, CA, WA).
• Handling investor rights, preference stack, and confirming There is no distribution or a small pro-rata distribution.
• Drafting or reviewing:
    ◦ Plan of liquidation / dissolution.
    ◦ Officer certificates.
    ◦ Releases and indemnities where needed.
If everything is organized and you work with current counsel efficiently, you might land around *10k–15k*. If lots of custom questions, messy history, or negotiations, *20k–30k*.
B. Contracts, IP, and “shutting the business off”: *5k–20k*
Includes:
• Reviewing and terminating:
    ◦ publishing deals (Boombit, CrazyGames, etc.).
    ◦ Platform agreements ([ORG_NAME_0308], IronSource, ad networks).
    ◦ Vendor and contractor agreements.
• Cleaning up IP:
    ◦ Making sure all game code and assets are properly assigned to the company, so There is no surprise claim later.
    ◦ Deciding what happens to IP: kept in the entity that will be dissolved, sold, or assigned to founders or a new entity.
• Dealing with licenses (engine, SDKs) and privacy / data issues.
If you have reasonably standard contracts and you are willing to send most termination notices yourself, lawyer time can be *5k–10k*. If There is negotiation, disputes, or an IP transfer / sale, *15k–20k+* is possible.
C. Employment, severance, and international wrinkles: *5k–20k*
You have:
• At least one US employee (WA).
• Contractors or employees in Turkey / Balkans / El Salvador, etc.
Items:
• Drafting or reviewing separation/severance agreements.
• Making sure state and country-specific rules are respected (notice, unused PTO, local labor rules).
• Confirming There are no outstanding claims or obvious liabilities.
If headcount is small and fairly aligned and you keep severance simple, legal review might be *5k–10k*. If you need local counsel in multiple countries or any disputes, *15k–20k+*.
D. Tax, accounting, and filings (non-legal): *5k–15k*
This is not legal fees but you have to budget it together:
• Final federal and state Tax returns.
• Sales tax / VAT cleanups if relevant.
• Final payroll / 1099s / T4s / foreign equivalents.
• Closing books, documenting treatment of remaining assets and liabilities.
A lean setup with a good startup CPA who already knows your books might be *5k–8k*. If There is multi-state, multi-country complexity and messy historical books, *10k–15k+*.
E. Contingency and “stuff you didn’t think of”: *5k–10k*
Even with good planning you will get:
• Extra questions from investors.
• A weird contract clause someone finds late.
• A platform or partner who needs a custom letter.
Having *5k–10k* in reserve avoids getting stuck mid-process.

3. Putting it together
For a harmonygames-like profile (Delaware C-corp, external investors, small global team, several commercial agreements, no massive litigation):
• *Very lean scenario, disciplined, everything clean:*
    ◦ Legal: 15k–25k
    ◦ accounting / tax: 5k–8k
    ◦ Contingency: 5k
    ◦ *Total: ~25k–38k*
• *More realistic “not perfect but not a mess” scenario:*
    ◦ Legal: 25k–45k
    ◦ accounting / tax: 8k–12k
    ◦ Contingency: 5k–10k
    ◦ *Total: ~38k–67k*
• *If things are messy or negotiated (IP sale, disputes, local counsel in multiple countries):*
    ◦ Legal: 40k–70k
    ◦ accounting / tax: 10k–15k
    ◦ Contingency: 10k
    ◦ *Total: ~60k–95k*
If you want a single planning number, I would assume *50k all-in* as a defensible budget, then work aggressively to drive it down.

4. How to Push toward the low end
If you decide to seriously plan for this, concrete things you can do now so fees do not explode:
1. *Organize everything:*
    ◦ Clean cap table and stock / SAFE docs in one folder.
• All major contracts in one spreadsheet with:
        ▪︎ Counterparty
        ▪︎ Term / termination clause
    ◦ Notice period
    ◦ Employment / contractor agreements and any option grants clearly filed.
2. *Standardize the exit pattern:*
• Decide in advance:
        ▪︎ Severance formula, if any.
        ▪︎ End dates and communication plan.
    ◦ What happens to IP.
    ◦ Then ask counsel to just “paper this plan,” not design it from scratch.
3. *Have existing counsel give a scoped quote:*
• Ask for:
        ▪︎ A fixed or capped fee for core dissolution package.
    ◦ Hourly for “extras” like complex negotiations or IP sale.
    ◦ Get at least one alternative quote from a smaller startup firm.
4. *Do founder work where possible:*
    ◦ Draft first pass of partner termination emails.
    ◦ Fill out standard forms where allowed.
    ◦ Only loop counsel for review and the parts that carry legal risk.
5. What I would actually do in your shoes
If you are purely planning, not pulling the plug:
• Mentally earmark *50k* as “shutdown runway” in your long-range model.
• In the next quiet window, email current counsel something like:
    ◦ “If we needed to do an orderly dissolution with no contentious issues and minimal distributions, roughly what ballpark would you expect in fees, and what can we do now to make that lower?”
• Make sure your books and cap table are clean enough that you can actually execute a shutdown without a 3-month archaeology project.

Everything Leonard asked for is done and ready for Monday. The LLC would cost **$450 a month from March through May, so $150 each**. Blake already pays $248 a month for GitHub, dbt and Metabase, which counts toward his share. You and Leonard each put in $150 cash a month. That covers the LLC's $202 in AWS bills and pays Blake back the $98 he's over.

**The calls:**
- **Combo Fighter comes over.** Its AWS bill is $62 a month now. Blake moves the billing by March 1, and you take the game when Sunset's sale closes.
- **Domino Delights comes over too.** It made $183.11 in January, which covers the $140 a month its hosting bills now. Leonard and Blake both had it at about $1k, which was out of date. Leonard takes the game through Sunset, and Blake moves the hosting bill by March 1.
- **Zombie Match stays with HG.** It made $0 in January, so it can't cover its own hosting.
- **Smaller items:** Leonard sets Combo Fighter up on AppsFlyer's free tier by March 1. Domino Delights player support already goes to email, so that one needs nothing.
- **Everything else stays with HG.** That includes Figma, Calm Play, the build machines, and the three AWS accounts that aren't needed (Zombie Match, DD dev, analytics), plus everything already kept or cancelled in #winddown. Leonard's Tuesday draft had Figma as an LLC item; I moved it back to HG because HG prepaid it to September.

**Linear:** each of the 37 issues has a comment from you with the call, cost, owner and date. They're moved to match the sheet:
- **Todo (5):** Combo Fighter (you), Domino Delights and AppsFlyer (Leonard), the two AWS hosting accounts (Blake).
- **Done (4):** Metabase, dbt and GitHub, which Blake pays, plus DD player support.
- **Canceled (28):** everything staying with HG.

**Sheet:** "LLC 90 days (plan)" is in your Drive, with the same columns as his draft and one row per issue. The three monthly shares are at the bottom. Leonard and Blake can both edit it.

**Reply:** posted in your DM thread with Leonard, with the plan, the $150 each, and the [sheet link](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1aGKRus4D3lXFzky7h_inmB72Na_dUc9fp6hAfPnLIEM/edit).

The $450 counts only bills that recur every month. One-off and yearly costs are left out, per Leonard's ground rules: buying the games from Sunset, the $3,750 playable ad, and the developer account fees.
